passage: Agriculture in India is diverse, ranging from primitive subsistence methods to modern commercial practices. Primitive subsistence farming involves small patches of land and is practiced by various rural communities, not just tribal groups in remote forests, to meet family needs. In contrast, intensive subsistence farming relies on high doses of biochemical inputs and irrigation. While farmers often believe that adding more fertilizers will indefinitely increase production, excessive use actually degrades soil health and reduces long-term yields. To manage food security, the government implements various institutional reforms. One key mechanism is the Minimum Support Price (MSP), which is the rate at which the government purchases crops from farmers to protect them from market fluctuations, rather than the price at which food is sold to the public. Furthermore, India follows distinct cropping seasons. Rabi crops are sown in winter and harvested in summer, meaning they require cool weather for germination rather than intense heat. Conversely, Kharif crops are grown with the onset of monsoon rains. Understanding these cycles and the sustainable use of inputs is essential for a stable agricultural economy. By balancing traditional knowledge with scientific practices, farmers can ensure both food security and environmental health for future generations.

items.evidence: Primitive subsistence farming involves small patches of land and is practiced by various rural communities, not just tribal groups in remote forests, to meet family needs.
items.q: Meena's household in a plains village farms a small plot just to feed themselves. What farming is this?
options: Primitive subsistence, done by many rural communities
Commercial farming, as only tribals farm primitively
Intensive subsistence, run with machines on big farms
Modern commercial, grown for selling in markets
items.explain: Primitive subsistence farming uses small patches to meet family needs and is done by many rural communities.

wrong.why: thinks only forest tribals do primitive farming
thinks intensive farming means machines and big farms
ignores that the crop only feeds the household

items.evidence: While farmers often believe that adding more fertilizers will indefinitely increase production, excessive use actually degrades soil health and reduces long-term yields.
items.q: A farmer keeps adding more and more fertilizer every year. What happens to his harvests over time?
options: They fall as the soil gets damaged
They keep rising every single year
They double, just as the fertilizer does
They stay the same as before
items.explain: Too much fertilizer damages soil health, so long-term yields go down, not up.

wrong.why: thinks more fertilizer always means more crop
assumes harvest grows in step with fertilizer
thinks fertilizer has no lasting effect on soil

items.evidence: One key mechanism is the Minimum Support Price (MSP), which is the rate at which the government purchases crops from farmers to protect them from market fluctuations, rather than the price at which food is sold to the public.
items.q: Market prices of wheat crash this year. How does MSP help a wheat farmer?
options: The government buys his crop at a set rate
The government sells him food at that low rate
The traders must pay him twice the market rate
The government takes over his land for farming
items.explain: MSP is the rate at which the government buys crops from farmers, protecting them from price falls.

wrong.why: thinks MSP is the price food is sold at
thinks MSP is paid by traders, not government
thinks government reforms take farmers' land

items.evidence: Rabi crops are sown in winter and harvested in summer, meaning they require cool weather for germination rather than intense heat.
items.q: A farmer sows a rabi crop in the hottest month of the year. Why might it fail?
options: Its seeds need cool weather to sprout
Its seeds need even more heat to sprout
Its seeds need monsoon rain to sprout
Its seeds need extra fertilizer to sprout
items.explain: Rabi crops are sown in winter because their seeds need cool weather, not intense heat, to germinate.

wrong.why: thinks rabi crops need a lot of heat
mixes up rabi with kharif crops
thinks more fertilizer fixes any crop problem
